newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador leader promises no economic shock treatment.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador leader promises no economic shock treatment.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon said his government's austerity package expected to be announced Monday would not include economic shock treatment.
"I've said I will aim for the least possible social impact. I don't want to apply shock treatment," Alarcon said in a meeting with foreign journalists Wednesday night.

The economic team is studying ways of plugging a $1.3 billion fiscal deficit and reducing it to between 2.5 percent and 2.7 percent of gross domestic product by the end of the year from the current 6.6 percent.
Alarcon was named interim president last February by the Congress after it ousted President Abdala Bucaram. The move came amid massive protests against Bucaram-imposed austerity measures.

Bucaram's economic measures, introduced to reach an International Monetary Fund (IMF) accord, aimed to cut state subsidies and raise electricity and gas rates by up to 200 percent and telephone tariffs by up to 600 percent.
Meeting with journalists on Wednesday night, Finance Minister Carlos Davalos said the government hoped to be able to announce new economic measures Monday.

"We understand that the economic situation of the people is not such that we they can bear measures that worsen it," Alarcon said. "The economic team is analyzing the outcome of policies applied so far and studying the likely impact of measures announced in the first days of our administration that have not yet been carried out."
The president, who took over an interim government three months ago, said he was satisfied with the level of international reserves, the exchange rate and interest rates.

The government has said it will not create new taxes to fight the fiscal deficit, but will try to make current laws more efficient, crack down on tax evasion and launch a tax lottery to encourage payments.
"The government wants to improve collection. It is not analyzing the creation of a new tax or the possibility of broadening the tax base," National Tax Director Carlos Velasco told Reuters.
Alarcon also said the government would meet all debt commitments this year.
Ecuador is waiting for the green light from the IMF Fund to start renegotiating its $1.2 billion debt with the Paris Club.
The country was $240 million in arrears on interest payments on its Paris Club debt in March.

"For the first time in many years Ecuador will be up-to-date in payments, including payments to the Paris Club," Alarcon said. "We have medium-term debts with the Paris Club that are due in July and December and we will meet these deadlines."
Ecuador's total foreign debt stands at more than $14.5 billion.
